title: Groupoïdes de Teichmüller et les S0 Tg,!ν, S0 TG : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp.108-111). G is a stable-graph or 'modular type'. M_G is the stratum of the Deligne-Mumford/Knudsen stack of curves of type G. G' is a generalization of G obtained by smoothing the set C of double points. SP_G is a rigidified Teichmuller-type cover with π1(SP_G) = ST_G, the Teichmuller group of type G.

The page continues the plumbing construction.
- M̃^C_G → M_G is the bundle of auxiliary choices: unit discs D_i at the two branches of each node in C, with equal radii ρ_α = ρ_ᾱ for the two orientations of an edge α.
- P̃^B_G → M̃^C_G is a U^B-torsor (written Γ_B / Γ̄_B over M_C on this page). Page 109 gives a cartesian square identifying it with the pull-back of SP_{G'} → M_{G'} along the plumbing map M̃^C_G → M_{G'}. Here X ↦ X' is the curve obtained by gluing along the annuli.

On p.109 Grothendieck introduces the multiplicative topological monoid ]0,1]^C, written m_C or M_{\vec C}. It acts on M̃^C_G by shrinking the discs. Combining the plumbing parameters with this action gives a map m_C × M̃^C_G → M_{G'}, which the dashed arrows factor through M̃^C_G. Because the monoid action is being quotiented in a homotopical sense, he calls it a 'morphisme de topos'.

It sits in a cartesian square: SP_{G'} pulled back along it is m_C × P^B_G. This 'morphism' plays the role of the inclusion into M_{G'} of the deleted tubular neighbourhood V*_{G,G'} of M_G in the closure M̂_{G'}; its intersection with M_{G'} is the punctured collar.

He then remarks this would be less intrinsic but clearer if M^C_G → M_G had a section. He asks whether one always exists and adds 'je pense que oui'. Given a section one gets a cartesian square SP_G × m_C → SP_{G'} over P_C × m_C → M_{G'}. Here P_C is (presumably) the torus bundle of tangential directions at the nodes, the 'bord' of the tubular neighbourhood (p.111: 'P_C × M_C s'identifie à une trace de voisinage tubulaire').

Purpose: to produce canonical (up to the torsor ambiguity) homomorphisms between Teichmuller groups ST_G → ST_{G'} attached to boundary strata, i.e. the 'gluing/inclusion' maps of the Teichmuller tower/groupoid. These are the topological counterpart of tangential base points at the boundary of M_{g,n}.
errors: Not a real error: the section question is left open ('y en a-t-il toujours ??'), but the answer is yes topologically. The fibres of M^C_G → M_G (choices of normalized discs/radii at the nodes) are contractible and the bundle is locally trivial over a paracompact orbifold, so continuous (equivariant) sections exist. Algebraically or holomorphically a global section need not exist; that is why Grothendieck calls the section version 'moins intrinsèque'.

Calling m_C × M̃^C_G → M_{G'} a 'morphisme de topos' is heuristic. As written it is a continuous map; the topos-level statement implicitly refers to the quotient by the monoid action (the dashed factorization), which is not made precise.
Notational slip inherited from p.109: 'la M_C-fibre M̃^C_C' should be M̃^C_G. Notation also wavers between M̃^C_G and M^C_G, and between P̃^B_G and P^B_G.

ideas.what: Plumbing map from (curve with nodes C + chosen discs) × (gluing parameters in ]0,1]^C) to the open stratum M_{G'}, as a model of the deleted tubular neighbourhood of the stratum M_G in M̄
ideas.modern_name: plumbing coordinates / Fenchel-Nielsen-type collar near the boundary; deleted neighbourhood of a boundary stratum
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Bers, Kra, Masur, Wolpert, Fay); Deligne-Mumford deformation theory
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2-3 discusses the Teichmuller tower and the need for 'tubular neighbourhoods' of strata, without this construction

ideas.what: Encoding the collar via an action of the multiplicative monoid ]0,1]^C and taking the topos-theoretic quotient, so the boundary torus bundle P_C × ]0,1]^C becomes the 'trace' of the tubular neighbourhood
ideas.modern_name: real oriented blow-up / Kato-Nakayama space of log-smooth DM compactification; log structure monoid
ideas.usually_credited_to: Kato-Nakayama (1999); real blow-up of M̄_{g,n} in Looijenga, Hatcher-Lochak-Schneps, Bakalov-Kirillov

ideas.what: Cartesian squares relating the Teichmuller covers SP_G, SP_{G'} over the collar, yielding homomorphisms ST_G → ST_{G'} between Teichmuller groups of a stratum and of its generalization
ideas.modern_name: boundary/gluing homomorphisms of mapping class groups; tangential base points; Teichmuller (Lego) groupoid
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), Teichmuller tower / Lego programme, stated informally

ideas.what: Existence of a global section of the disc-choice bundle M^C_G → M_G to trivialize the construction

missed.claim: Grothendieck models the deleted tubular neighbourhood of a boundary stratum of M̄_{g,ν} by an action of the multiplicative monoid ]0,1]^C (one factor per node to be smoothed) on the bundle of disc choices, quotiented at the topos level. The boundary torus bundle P_C × ]0,1]^C is the 'trace' of the tubular neighbourhood. This is essentially the structure later formalized by log geometry and the Kato-Nakayama real blow-up, which is exactly what is used to define tangential base points and boundary homomorphisms of Teichmuller groupoids. That this monoid/topos formulation predates log geometry (c.1978-81) seems unrecorded.
missed.quote: Considérons le monoïde topologique multiplicatif ]0,1] ... On a donc un morphisme de topos M_C × M̃^C_G → M_{G'} ... joue le rôle de l'"inclusion" du voisinage V*_{G,G'}
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Historical credit: a precursor of the Kato-Nakayama/log approach to the Teichmuller tower in Grothendieck's own notes. It also suggests a topos-theoretic, monoid-quotient formulation of boundary maps of Teichmuller groupoids that is not standard.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (plumbing, collars, boundary homomorphisms of mapping class groups) is classical, and its role in the Teichmuller tower is announced in the Esquisse. The mildly notable detail is the monoid ]0,1]^C / topos-morphism formalism for the deleted tubular neighbourhood, an early informal anticipation of the Kato-Nakayama real blow-up viewpoint. It is left heuristic and unfinished.
transcription_corrections: The symbol transcribed '𝓜_C' / 'M_C' in the diagrams is Grothendieck's notation for the monoid ]0,1]^{\vec C} introduced on p.109 (written m_{\vec C} with an arrow over C). It should be distinguished from the stratum M_G.
First line: roughly 'donc ... sur P̃^B_G, ... torseur sous Γ_B (superscript: U^B-tors.) sur M_C'; the over-line insertion reads 'U^B-tors.'.
In the first cartesian square the left vertical arrow is decorated with '≀ ~' (torsor/isomorphism mark), and the bottom-left object is M_C × M^C_G (tilde possibly omitted).
'voisinage V*_{G,G'} ... (trace sur M_{G'} du voisinage tubulaire de M_G dans M̂_{G'}) dans M_{G'}' — the inserted words are 'trace' and 'tubulaire'.
Marginal note at the section question reads 'je pense que oui...', inserted next to '(y en a-t-il toujours ??)'.
Last diagram: SP_G × m_C → SP_{G'} over P_C × m_C → M_{G'}.
